findings.evidence: `DiagonalizableGroup.Basic` defines its analogous `pointsMulEquiv` and `pointsMulEquiv_mapValue` under `[CommSemiring A]` and `[CommSemiring B]`; lines 123–136 and 203–209 here use only `AlgHom.mapDomain`, evaluation, and `AlgHom.mapValue_mapDomain`.
findings.fix: Put these three declarations in a `[CommSemiring A]`/`[CommSemiring B]` section, and introduce `[CommRing A]` only for the matrix-comparison theorems requiring `GeneralLinear.pointsMulEquiv`.
findings.issue: The section-wide `[CommRing A]` and line 200 `[CommRing B]` overconstrain `determinantPoints`, `determinantPoints_apply_apply`, and `mapValue_determinantPoints`; these declarations only use pre/postcomposition of algebra maps and convolution.

summary: The point-map API is unnecessarily restricted to ring-valued algebras even where only commutative semirings are required.
